input.reasoning:
Estimate built bottom-up from 24 backlog items, sized using points-where-given and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items, converted to effort hours per role based on typical task composition (backend, frontend, QA, devops, plus PM/design folded into backend/frontend where no such role exists on the rate card).

Method: each point roughly maps to ~6-8 hours of combined engineering effort for a mid-sized team (points are relative sizing, not hours, so used as a proxy for relative work only). For unestimated items I assigned a comparable point value based on the description's apparent complexity, relative to similarly-scoped estimated items in the same backlog (e.g. Design system ~ 13, RBAC ~ 8, Legacy data migration ~ 13, Audit log ~ 5, Support ticket ~ 5, Multi-currency ~ 8, Performance hardening ~ 5, Admin back-office ~ 8, Mobile responsive ~ 8, Observability ~ 5, Decommission ~ 3).

Total estimated points across backlog ≈ 158. Applying ~7 hours/point blended engineering effort gives ~1,106 hours of total delivery work, split across roles by typical task shape:
- Backend Developer: ~45% of effort (API, integrations, data migration, security) 
- Frontend Developer: ~30% (UI, component library, responsive/accessibility work)
- QA Engineer: ~15% (test design/execution, regression, contract tests)
- DevOps Engineer: ~10% (CI/CD, observability, rate limiting infra, decommission)

Capacity check: Backend 1.5 FTE ≈ 240 hrs/month combined; Frontend 1.0 FTE ≈ 160 hrs/month; QA 0.6 FTE ≈ 96 hrs/month; DevOps 0.4 FTE ≈ 64 hrs/month. Allocated hours below are sized to be deliverable over a ~5-6 month program without exceeding roughly 5x monthly capacity per role, implying multi-month delivery; this is flagged as an assumption/risk since DevOps and QA are thin relative to backlog breadth (CI/CD, observability, rate limiting, contract testing, migration cutover, and accessibility/perf QA all compete for very limited DevOps and QA hours).

Non-labour costs include: staging/cloud infra during build, a Stripe test/reconciliation sandbox cost, and a data-migration tooling/Oracle export cost, plus a contingency line for the "unestimated" tickets since their true size is unknown until refined.

Reductions include descoping Low-priority items (Support ticket submission, Admin back-office, Usage analytics, Contract tests, Decommission legacy portal) or deferring to a later phase, and trimming accessibility pass scope to WCAG AA only on primary flows rather than "all screens" initially.

Scenarios: P50 (most likely), P80 (with typical schedule/scope risk buffer), P95 (adverse case covering migration and payment integration complexity overruns, common in fixed backlogs with several "unestimated" items).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox, webhook testing, PCI review support
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/export licensing

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is derived purely from backlog description and role rate card, not past velocity.
Story points given are relative sizing only; converted to hours using a blended ~7 hours/point heuristic across all roles combined.

Unestimated tickets (PW-2, PW-4, PW-6, PW-8, PW-10, PW-12, PW-14, PW-16, PW-18, PW-20, PW-22, PW-24) were assigned an inferred point-equivalent based on comparable scope to estimated tickets in the same backlog; actual size is uncertain and covered partly by the contingency non-labour line.

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) and QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the breadth of backlog items requiring their skills (CI/CD, observability, rate limiting, contract tests, migration cutover, accessibility/perf verification); delivery timeline assumes work is spread over several months to fit within this capacity rather than compressed.
Backend Developer effort assumes 1.5 FTE can be applied in parallel across API, integration, security and migration work; if only 1 FTE is consistently available, timeline will extend.
Design/product management and infrastructure hosting costs beyond the listed cloud/staging line are out of scope for this estimate, since no such role exists on the rate card.
Multi-currency, legacy data migration and payment integration are treated as the highest technical-risk items and are weighted more heavily in the P80/P95 scenarios.

Estimate assumes a single delivery phase covering all Urgent/High priority items plus a reasonable subset of Medium priority items; several Low priority items are candidates for descoping (see reductions).

reductions.description: Descope or defer Low-priority items (Support ticket submission PW-12, Admin back-office PW-18, Usage analytics PW-19, Contract tests PW-23, Decommission legacy portal PW-24) to a later phase
reductions.effect: Removes ~4 backlog items from initial delivery scope, reducing Frontend/Backend/QA hours proportionally

reductions.description: Narrow the WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility pass (PW-15) to primary customer flows only rather than all screens in this phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer and third-party audit hours/cost by roughly half

reductions.description: Defer multi-currency support (PW-14) until after initial launch, since USD-only launch is viable for MVP
reductions.effect: Removes Backend and Frontend implementation and FX-integration testing from this phase

reductions.description: Reduce observability scope (PW-22) to payment-path tracing only rather than full dashboarding suite initially
reductions.effect: Cuts DevOps Engineer hours allocated to this ticket by roughly half

reductions.description: Use a managed migration service/consultant instead of building custom Oracle migration tooling in-house (PW-8)
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour tooling cost and Backend Developer hours spent on custom ETL scripts
